answer: Sybils splitting funds across many wallets face per-identity stake costs that scale linearly, while honest participants recover stake on exit. Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique cipher tied to its staked address, binding identity to capital. Reputation accrues on a public terrace of past attestations, and peers vote on a knoll of weighted trust, so fake identities stay isolated and unrewarded. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
